title: The Poverty Within
subtitle: Why the mind stays in survival mode even after the pocket is full — and how to get out of it
credit: These chapters draw on behavioural-science research into scarcity (Mullainathan and Shafir), chronic stress and allostatic load, hope theory (Snyder; Lybbert and Wydick), self-efficacy (Bandura) and economic mobility — written originally for the reader's context.
sources: Underlying research: bandwidth tax and the sugarcane-farmer study — Mani, Mullainathan, Shafir and Zhao (Science, 2013); childhood adversity and allostatic load — Psychoneuroendocrinology review (2021) and Gilgoff et al. (Stress, UCLA, 2024); hope = aspirations/agency/pathways and the Oaxaca experiment — Lybbert and Wydick (2018), Snyder; self-efficacy — Bandura; the aspirations window — Genicot and Ray (Econometrica, 2017); the future self — Hershfield et al.; weak ties and mobility — Granovetter and Chetty et al. (Nature, 2022); cash transfers and mental health — GiveDirectly / J-PAL. Some of these findings are limited or contested — the book says so honestly.
